title: RF exposure, grounding and tower safety
blurb: Explain what limits protect the public, who is responsible, why microwave beams matter, and how to tie off and ground safely.

E0A01.why: A ground rod gives lightning's charge a path into the earth: **lightning charge dissipation**.
E0A01.trap: Static on power lines, RF between equipment and the breaker panel are not its primary job.

E0A02.why: Neighbors are the general public, so you meet the **uncontrolled** limits. The term is maximum permissible **exposure**.
E0A02.trap: Controlled limits apply to aware, trained people. "Emission" is the wrong word.

E0A03.why: The body absorbs RF most readily at **30 – 300 MHz**, so the limits are tightest there.

E0A04.why: Each transmitter making **5 percent or more of its MPE limit** where the total is exceeded must help mitigate.

E0A05.why: The hazard is **high-gain antennas** focusing power into a narrow beam, so exposure inside it can be high.
E0A05.trap: Microwaves are non-ionizing, and wave velocity doesn't change.

E0A06.why: The body reacts to both fields, reflections vary the field, and E and H peaks sit in different places. **All of these** apply.

E0A07.why: 100% tie-off means **at least one lanyard attached to the tower at all times**.

E0A08.why: SAR is **the rate at which RF energy is absorbed by the body**, in watts per kilogram.

E0A09.why: The pool's exemption is **hand-held transceivers sold before May 3, 2021**.
E0A09.trap: Low watts or a small dish do not exempt you.

E0A10.why: The exam's answer: an evaluation **must always be performed**. Mode, ERP and power are not reasons to skip it.

E0A11.why: Lanyards clip to the **tower legs**, the strong structural members.
E0A11.trap: Rungs, masts and guy brackets aren't built to catch a fall.

E0A12.why: Attach the shock-absorbing lanyard **above head level**, so any fall is short.
E0A12.trap: Waist-level or low attachment lets you fall farther.
